claim: A selective code generator that abstains based on fuzz-generated unit-test correctness controls the false discovery rate of code errors (FDR-CE) with statistical guarantees.
stance_target: L3: selective generation / abstention with risk control on code
scope_conditions: i.i.d. assumption; GPT-4o, Gemini-1.5 Pro, DeepSeek R1, CodeLlama 13B Instruct
quoted_support: We propose a selective code generator that abstains from uncertain generations - based on the functional correctness evaluated by generated unit tests - to theoretically control the correctness among non-abstained answers, i.e., the false discovery rate.

claim: Evaluation uses fuzzing-generated tests (APPS-f, Mercury-f, HumanEval-f, MBPP-f) replacing built-in tests for both learning and evaluation, a different label regime from hidden benchmark tests.
quoted_support: We construct APPS-f, Mercury-f, HumanEval-f, and MBPP-f, where for each dataset, we replace the built in unit tests from each problem with automatically generated unit tests via fuzzing for both learning and evaluation.
